<!-- lemma-1: body_md -->
\label{lem:shape-quotient}
Let $\mathcal H$ be a group object of $\textbf{H}$ acting on a pointed object $\mathcal{X}$, and define
$\mathsf H:=
  \raisebox{1pt}{\rm\normalfont\textesh}
\mathcal H$.
The natural equivalence (cf.\ Remark~\ref{rmk:shape-groupoid})
\begin{equation}
    
  \raisebox{1pt}{\rm\normalfont\textesh}
(\mathcal{X}
  \IfBooleanTF{#1}
    {\big/\mkern-7mu\big/}
    {/\mkern-6mu/}
{\mathcal H})\cong(
  \raisebox{1pt}{\rm\normalfont\textesh}
\mathcal{X})
  \IfBooleanTF{#1}
    {\big/\mkern-7mu\big/}
    {/\mkern-6mu/}
\mathsf H,
\end{equation}
is equivalently a colimit over a diagram
\begin{equation}
    
  \raisebox{1pt}{\rm\normalfont\textesh}
(\mathcal{X}
  \IfBooleanTF{#1}
    {\big/\mkern-7mu\big/}
    {/\mkern-6mu/}
{\mathcal H})\cong\mathrm{colim}_{\mathbf{B}\mathsf H}
  \raisebox{1pt}{\rm\normalfont\textesh}
\mathcal{X}.
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-1 -->
<!-- proof-3: body_md -->
By definition, the homotopy quotient $\mathcal{X} 
  \IfBooleanTF{#1}
    {\big/\mkern-7mu\big/}
    {/\mkern-6mu/}
 \mathcal{H}$ is the geometric realization of the action groupoid
\begin{equation}
    \mathcal{X}
  \IfBooleanTF{#1}
    {\big/\mkern-7mu\big/}
    {/\mkern-6mu/}
{\mathcal H}=\left|\,[k]\longmapsto \mathcal{X}\times\mathcal H^{\times k}\,\right|.
\end{equation}
Since $
  \raisebox{1pt}{\rm\normalfont\textesh}
$ is a left adjoint, it preserves these geometric realizations. The object $\mathsf H=
  \raisebox{1pt}{\rm\normalfont\textesh}
\mathcal H$ is a group object in $\textbf{H}$, and the cohesion axioms imply that $
  \raisebox{1pt}{\rm\normalfont\textesh}
$ preserves finite products. Therefore $
  \raisebox{1pt}{\rm\normalfont\textesh}
$ carries the action groupoid levelwise to
\begin{equation}
    [k]\longmapsto 
  \raisebox{1pt}{\rm\normalfont\textesh}
\mathcal{X}\times(
  \raisebox{1pt}{\rm\normalfont\textesh}
\mathcal H)^{\times k}
    =
  \raisebox{1pt}{\rm\normalfont\textesh}
\mathcal{X}\times\mathsf H^{\times k}.
\end{equation}
Since compatibility with the face and degeneracy maps holds, we have
\begin{equation}\label{eq:shape-quotient-colim}
    
  \raisebox{1pt}{\rm\normalfont\textesh}
(\mathcal{X}
  \IfBooleanTF{#1}
    {\big/\mkern-7mu\big/}
    {/\mkern-6mu/}
{\mathcal H})\cong\left|\,[k]\longmapsto
  \raisebox{1pt}{\rm\normalfont\textesh}
\mathcal{X}\times\mathsf H^{\times k}\,\right|=(
  \raisebox{1pt}{\rm\normalfont\textesh}
\mathcal{X})
  \IfBooleanTF{#1}
    {\big/\mkern-7mu\big/}
    {/\mkern-6mu/}
\mathsf H\cong\mathrm{colim}_{\mathbf{B}\mathsf H}
  \raisebox{1pt}{\rm\normalfont\textesh}
\mathcal{X}.
\end{equation}
Since $\mathsf H=
  \raisebox{1pt}{\rm\normalfont\textesh}
\mathcal H$ is discrete, $\mathsf H=\mathrm{Dsc}(K)$ for an $\infty$-group $K$, and $\mathbf B\mathsf H=\mathrm{Dsc}(BK)=\mathrm{colim}_{BK}*$. By descent (cf.\ \cite[Proposition~4.3.8]{Sati_Schreiber_2026}, \cite[Lemma~3.10]{BeardsleyPeroux2022}), $\textbf{H}_{/\mathbf B\mathsf H}\cong\lim_{BK}\textbf{H}_{/*}\cong\mathrm{Fun}(BK,\textbf{H})$, under which an $\mathsf H$-action on an object corresponds to a functor $BK\to\textbf{H}$ and the homotopy quotient to its colimit. This identifies $(
  \raisebox{1pt}{\rm\normalfont\textesh}
\mathcal{X})
  \IfBooleanTF{#1}
    {\big/\mkern-7mu\big/}
    {/\mkern-6mu/}
\mathsf H$ with $\mathrm{colim}_{\mathbf B\mathsf H}
  \raisebox{1pt}{\rm\normalfont\textesh}
\mathcal{X}$ in \eqref{eq:shape-quotient-colim}.
<!-- end proof-3 -->
<!-- lemma-2: body_md -->
\label{lem:mapping-colimit}
For every diagram $i\mapsto A_i$ in $\textbf{H}$ and every $\mathcal{T}\in\mathrm{ob}\,\textbf{H}$, there is a natural equivalence
\begin{equation}
    [\mathrm{colim}_i A_i,\mathcal{T}]\cong\lim_i[A_i,\mathcal{T}].
\end{equation}
In particular, we have that
\begin{equation}
    [
  \raisebox{1pt}{\rm\normalfont\textesh}
(\mathcal{X}
  \IfBooleanTF{#1}
    {\big/\mkern-7mu\big/}
    {/\mkern-6mu/}
{\mathcal H}),\mathcal{T}]\cong[
  \raisebox{1pt}{\rm\normalfont\textesh}
\mathcal{X},\mathcal{T}]^{h\mathsf H}.
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-2 -->
<!-- proof-4: body_md -->
For every $B\in\mathrm{ob}\,\textbf{H}$, Cartesian closedness gives
\begin{align}
    \textbf{H}\left(B,[\mathrm{colim}_i A_i,\mathcal{T}]\right)
    &\cong \textbf{H}\left(B\times\mathrm{colim}_i A_i,\mathcal{T}\right)
    \cong \textbf{H}\left(\mathrm{colim}_i(B\times A_i),\mathcal{T}\right)\notag\\
    &\cong \lim_i\textbf{H}(B\times A_i,\mathcal{T})
    \cong \lim_i\textbf{H}(B,[A_i,\mathcal{T}]),
\end{align}
which by Yoneda implies that $[\mathrm{colim}_i A_i,\mathcal{T}]\cong\lim_i[A_i,\mathcal{T}]$. Applying this to Lemma~\ref{lem:shape-quotient} gives
\begin{equation}
    [
  \raisebox{1pt}{\rm\normalfont\textesh}
(\mathcal{X}
  \IfBooleanTF{#1}
    {\big/\mkern-7mu\big/}
    {/\mkern-6mu/}
{\mathcal H}),\mathcal{T}]\cong\lim_{\mathbf{B}\mathsf H}[
  \raisebox{1pt}{\rm\normalfont\textesh}
\mathcal{X},\mathcal{T}]=[
  \raisebox{1pt}{\rm\normalfont\textesh}
\mathcal{X},\mathcal{T}]^{h\mathsf H}.
\end{equation}
<!-- end proof-4 -->
<!-- remark-25: body_md -->
\label{rmk:limits-underlying}
    When $\mathcal{T}$ is a grouplike $E_\infty$-object, so is $[
  \raisebox{1pt}{\rm\normalfont\textesh}
\mathcal{X},\mathcal{T}]$, and the
    limit above may be formed either in $\textbf{H}$ or in
    $\mathrm{Grp}_{E_\infty}(\textbf{H})$. In particular, limits of $E_\infty$-objects are created by
    the forgetful functor to $\textbf{H}$. The two readings of
    $[
  \raisebox{1pt}{\rm\normalfont\textesh}
\mathcal{X},\mathcal{T}]^{h\mathsf H}$ therefore agree. In what follows, we will exploit this \textit{additional structure} on the mapping stack. In other words, we find that it is \textit{convenient} to take into account the composition structure on the mapping stack (and implicitly on $\mathrm{Mag}_\mathcal{T}(\mathcal{X})$), though strictly speaking it is not \textit{necessary} for the general theory (see Remark~\ref{rmk:hypotheses-fibration}). That being said, in specific applications, an adequate composition structure is in fact \textit{necessary} to reproduce many results expected on physical grounds, as we discuss in the upcoming \cite{PerezLona:applications}.
<!-- end remark-25 -->
<!-- remark-26: body_md -->
\label{rmk:precomposition-action}
    The $\mathsf H$-action on $[
  \raisebox{1pt}{\rm\normalfont\textesh}
\mathcal{X},\mathcal{T}]$ is induced by
    precomposition:
    \begin{equation}
        \gamma\longmapsto(\gamma^{-1})^*.
    \end{equation}
But notice that it is not necessarily an action by \textit{pointed} automorphisms, so in particular \textit{the basepoint of $
  \raisebox{1pt}{\rm\normalfont\textesh}
 \mathcal{X}$ is not necessarily preserved}. This is a crucial point, as it implies that the sequence that defines the target space of magnetic symmetry backgrounds
\begin{equation}
    \mathrm{Mag}_\mathcal{T}(\mathcal{X}) \longrightarrow [
  \raisebox{1pt}{\rm\normalfont\textesh}
\mathcal{X},\mathcal{T}] \longrightarrow \mathcal{T}
\end{equation}
is not $\mathsf H$-equivariant, and thus operations concerning the $\mathsf{H}$-action, notably the computation of fixed stacks we shall employ, need not respect the sequence. Therefore, we will use a different, \textit{equivariant} way to define the magnetic symmetry background target space. For this, denote
\begin{equation}
    A:=
  \raisebox{1pt}{\rm\normalfont\textesh}
\mathcal{X},
    \quad
    M:=[A,\mathcal{T}].
\end{equation}
The terminal map $!:A\to *$ is automatically $\mathsf H$-equivariant, with $*$ equipped with the trivial $\mathsf{H}$-action. It therefore induces a canonical equivariant map
\begin{equation}
    s:=\mathrm{const}=[!,\mathcal{T}]:
    \mathcal{T}=[*,\mathcal{T}]\longrightarrow[A,\mathcal{T}]=M,
\end{equation}
where $\mathcal{T}$ carries the trivial $\mathsf H$-action.
<!-- end remark-26 -->
<!-- definition-6: body_md -->
\label{def:reduced}
    We define the \textit{reduced} object  in $\mathrm{Fun}(\mathbf{B}\mathsf H,\mathrm{Grp}_{E_\infty}(\textbf{H}))$ as
    \begin{equation}
        M_{\mathrm{red}}:=[A,\mathcal{T}]_{\mathrm{red}}
        :=\mathrm{cofib}\left(\mathcal{T}\xrightarrow{s}M\right).
    \end{equation}
<!-- end definition-6 -->
<!-- lemma-3: body_md -->
\label{lem:stable-retract}
    Let $\mathcal C$ be a stable $\infty$-category and let
    \begin{equation}
        r:M\to\mathcal{T},
        \quad
        s:\mathcal{T}\to M
    \end{equation}
    be morphisms of $\mathcal C$ equipped with an equivalence $
        rs\cong\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal{T}}.$   For $F:=\mathrm{fib}(r)$, with fiber inclusion $j:F\to M$, we have that
    \begin{equation}
\varphi:=j\,\mathrm{pr}_F+s\,\mathrm{pr}_{\mathcal{T}}:
        F\oplus\mathcal{T}\longrightarrow M
    \end{equation}
    is an equivalence. Under $\varphi$, the map $s$ is the inclusion of
    the summand $\mathcal{T}$ and $r$ is the projection onto it, giving an equivalence
    \begin{equation}
        \mathrm{cofib}(s)\cong F=\mathrm{fib}(r).
    \end{equation}
    Since the construction uses only $\mathrm{fib}$, $\oplus$, and the given data, it
    is functorial in the quadruple $(M,\mathcal{T},r,s)$ and applies verbatim in
    $\mathrm{Fun}(K,\mathcal C)$ for any simplicial set $K$ \cite[Proposition 1.1.3.1]{lurie2017higher}.
<!-- end lemma-3 -->
<!-- proof-5: body_md -->
From $rs\cong\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal{T}}$ and $rj\cong0$ we get
    \begin{equation}
        r\varphi
        =
        rj\,\mathrm{pr}_F+rs\,\mathrm{pr}_{\mathcal{T}}
        \cong
        \mathrm{pr}_{\mathcal{T}}.
    \end{equation}
    Since moreover $\varphi|_F=j$, there is a commutative diagram of fiber sequences
    \begin{equation}
    \begin{tikzcd}
        F \arrow[r] \arrow[d, equal] & F\oplus\mathcal{T} \arrow[r, "\mathrm{pr}_{\mathcal{T}}"] \arrow[d, "\varphi"] & \mathcal{T} \arrow[d, equal] \\
        F \arrow[r, "j"'] & M \arrow[r, "r"'] & \mathcal{T}.
    \end{tikzcd}
    \end{equation}
    Both rows are split fiber sequences, so this is a map of
    distinguished triangles in the homotopy category of $\mathcal C$, and
    $\varphi$ is an equivalence by the five lemma. Under this equivalence $s$ corresponds to the inclusion of
    the $\mathcal{T}$-summand, whose cofiber is $F$. Since $\mathrm{Fun}(K,\mathcal C)$ is
    stable with pointwise fibers, cofibers, and biproducts, the same
    construction applies there.
<!-- end proof-5 -->
<!-- lemma-4: body_md -->
\label{lem:connectivity}
    Let $M,\mathcal{T}\in\mathrm{ob}\,\mathrm{Sp}^{\mathrm{cn}}(\textbf{H})$ be connective spectrum objects in $\textbf{H}$ (Definition~\ref{app:def:conn-spec}) and let $r,s$ be as in Lemma~\ref{lem:stable-retract}. Then:
    \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
        \item the cofiber of $s$ formed in $\mathrm{Sp}^{\mathrm{cn}}(\textbf{H})$ agrees with the
        cofiber formed in $\mathrm{Sp}(\textbf{H})$, and so it is connective too,
        \item the fiber formed in $\mathrm{Sp}(\textbf{H})$ is connective, hence agrees
        with the fiber formed in $\mathrm{Sp}^{\mathrm{cn}}(\textbf{H})$.
    \end{enumerate}
    Hence, the equivalences of Lemma~\ref{lem:stable-retract} hold
    in $\mathrm{Sp}^{\mathrm{cn}}(\textbf{H})\cong\mathrm{Grp}_{E_\infty}(\textbf{H})$, and, pointwise, in
    $\mathrm{Fun}(K,\mathrm{Sp}^{\mathrm{cn}}(\textbf{H}))$.
<!-- end lemma-4 -->
<!-- proof-6: body_md -->
The inclusion $i:\mathrm{Sp}^{\mathrm{cn}}(\textbf{H})\hookrightarrow\mathrm{Sp}(\textbf{H})$ is a left adjoint, with right adjoint $\tau_{\geq0}$ the truncation functor (Definition~\ref{app:def:truncation-functors-spec}). Hence, it preserves colimits. This gives (a), and the cofiber is a colimit
    of connective objects, hence connective.

    For (b), the long exact sequence of homotopy sheaves of
    \begin{equation}
        \mathrm{fib}(r)\to M\xrightarrow{r}\mathcal{T}
    \end{equation}
    gives $\pi_n\mathrm{fib}(r)=0$ for $n\leq-2$, since $\pi_nM$ and
    $\pi_{n+1}\mathcal{T}$ vanish there. Further, we have the equivalence $\pi_{-1}\mathrm{fib}(r)\cong\mathrm{coker}\left(\pi_0(r)\right)$ with the cokernel constructed in abelian group objects of $\textbf{H}$. Now, since
    $\pi_0(r)\pi_0(s)=\mathrm{id}$, $\pi_0(r)$ is a split epimorphism
    of sheaves of abelian groups, hence an epimorphism, which gives that the cokernel
    vanishes. We conclude that $\mathrm{fib}(r)$ is connective and
    $\tau_{\geq0}\mathrm{fib}(r)=\mathrm{fib}(r)$.

    Finally, colimits, limits, and truncations in $\mathrm{Fun}(K,-)$ are computed
    pointwise, so both statements follow.
<!-- end proof-6 -->
<!-- corollary-2: body_md -->
\label{cor:red-pointed}
    Let $A$ be pointed by $a: *\to A$ and let $\mathcal{T}$ be a grouplike
    $E_\infty$-object. Let
    \begin{equation}
        M=[A,\mathcal{T}],\quad
        s=\mathrm{const}:\mathcal{T}\to M,\quad
        r=\mathrm{ev}_a:M\to\mathcal{T}.
    \end{equation}
    Then $rs=\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal{T}}$, and there is an equivalence
    \begin{equation}
        \mathrm{cofib}(s)\cong\mathrm{fib}(r)=[A,\mathcal{T}]_{*,a}
    \end{equation}
    in $\mathrm{Grp}_{E_\infty}(\textbf{H})$ (i.e. an equivalence, but not necessarily equivariant, since only one of them carries an $\mathsf{H}$-action with the present hypotheses).
<!-- end corollary-2 -->
<!-- proof-7: body_md -->
The identity $rs=\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal{T}}$ follows from
    \begin{equation}
        rs=[\,!\circ a,\mathcal{T}]=[\mathrm{id}_*,\mathcal{T}]=\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal{T}},
    \end{equation}
    where the composite is indexed by $!\circ a=\mathrm{id}_*$ because
    $[-,\mathcal{T}]$ is contravariant. Both $M$ and $\mathcal{T}$ are connective, so
    Lemmas~\ref{lem:stable-retract} and \ref{lem:connectivity} apply.
<!-- end proof-7 -->
<!-- lemma-5: body_md -->
\label{lem:equivariant-reduced}
    There is a fiber sequence 
    \begin{equation}
        \mathcal{T}\xrightarrow{\mathrm{const}}
        [
  \raisebox{1pt}{\rm\normalfont\textesh}
\mathcal{X},\mathcal{T}]
        \longrightarrow
        [
  \raisebox{1pt}{\rm\normalfont\textesh}
\mathcal{X},\mathcal{T}]_{\mathrm{red}}
    \end{equation}
   in
$ \mathrm{Fun}(\mathbf{B}\mathsf H,\mathrm{Grp}_{E_\infty}(\textbf{H}))$. No point of $\mathcal{X}$ is used. The sequence need not be equivariantly
    split.
<!-- end lemma-5 -->
<!-- proof-8: body_md -->
By Definition~\ref{def:reduced}, the sequence is a cofiber
    sequence in $\mathrm{Fun}(\mathbf{B}\mathsf H,\mathrm{Sp}^{\mathrm{cn}}(\textbf{H}))$. Colimits in functor
    categories are pointwise and the inclusion
    $i:\mathrm{Sp}^{\mathrm{cn}}(\textbf{H})\hookrightarrow\mathrm{Sp}(\textbf{H})$ preserves colimits, so it is
    also a cofiber sequence in $\mathrm{Fun}(\mathbf{B}\mathsf H,\mathrm{Sp}(\textbf{H}))$. The latter is
    stable, so the sequence is there a fiber sequence as well.

    All three terms are connective. Since the fiber formed in
    $\mathrm{Fun}(\mathbf{B}\mathsf H,\mathrm{Sp}^{\mathrm{cn}}(\textbf{H}))$ is $\tau_{\geq0}$ of the stable fiber,
    and $\tau_{\geq0}\mathcal{T}=\mathcal{T}$, the sequence is a fiber sequence in
    $\mathrm{Fun}(\mathbf{B}\mathsf H,\mathrm{Grp}_{E_\infty}(\textbf{H}))$.

    The non-equivariant splitting need not be equivariant, as we exemplify in Section~\ref{sssec:pin2}.
<!-- end proof-8 -->
<!-- lemma-6: body_md -->
\label{lem:hfp-reduced}
    Let
    \begin{equation}
        Q:=\left([
  \raisebox{1pt}{\rm\normalfont\textesh}
\mathcal{X},\mathcal{T}]_{\mathrm{red}}\right)^{h\mathsf H}.
    \end{equation}
    Then there is a fiber sequence
    \begin{equation}
        [\mathbf{B}\mathsf H,\mathcal{T}]
        \xrightarrow{\,p^*\,}
        [
  \raisebox{1pt}{\rm\normalfont\textesh}
(\mathcal{X}
  \IfBooleanTF{#1}
    {\big/\mkern-7mu\big/}
    {/\mkern-6mu/}
{\mathcal H}),\mathcal{T}]
        \longrightarrow Q,
    \end{equation}
    where $p:
  \raisebox{1pt}{\rm\normalfont\textesh}
(\mathcal{X}
  \IfBooleanTF{#1}
    {\big/\mkern-7mu\big/}
    {/\mkern-6mu/}
{\mathcal H})\longrightarrow\mathbf{B}\mathsf H$
    is the canonical projection.
<!-- end lemma-6 -->
<!-- proof-9: body_md -->
We apply $(-)^{h\mathsf H}=\lim_{\mathbf{B}\mathsf H}$ to the fiber sequence of Lemma~\ref{lem:equivariant-reduced}. Since
    limits preserve fiber sequences, and limits in $\mathrm{Grp}_{E_\infty}(\textbf{H})$ are created in $\textbf{H}$ (Remark~\ref{rmk:limits-underlying}), this gives a fiber sequence
    \begin{equation}
        \mathcal{T}^{h\mathsf H}
        \longrightarrow
        [
  \raisebox{1pt}{\rm\normalfont\textesh}
\mathcal{X},\mathcal{T}]^{h\mathsf H}
        \longrightarrow Q.
    \end{equation}

    Let $D_{\mathcal{X}}$ denote the
    $\mathsf H$-diagram with value $
  \raisebox{1pt}{\rm\normalfont\textesh}
\mathcal{X}$, and let $D_*$ denote the
    constant diagram with value $*$. The terminal maps
$        \alpha_i=\,!:
  \raisebox{1pt}{\rm\normalfont\textesh}
\mathcal{X}\to *
$    assemble into a natural transformation $\alpha:D_{\mathcal{X}}\Rightarrow D_*$, and $\mathrm{const}=[\alpha_i,\mathcal{T}]$ is equivariant because $\alpha$ is. By Lemma~\ref{lem:shape-quotient}, natural in the $\mathcal H$-object $\mathcal{X}$, taking colimits gives
    \begin{equation}
        \mathrm{colim} D_{\mathcal{X}}=
  \raisebox{1pt}{\rm\normalfont\textesh}
(\mathcal{X}
  \IfBooleanTF{#1}
    {\big/\mkern-7mu\big/}
    {/\mkern-6mu/}
{\mathcal H}),
        \quad
        \mathrm{colim} D_* = \mathbf{B}\mathsf H,

<!-- lemma-11: body_md -->
\label{lem:stable-connective-hfp}
    Let
    \begin{equation}
        M=[
  \raisebox{1pt}{\rm\normalfont\textesh}
\mathcal{X},\mathcal{T}]\in\mathrm{ob}\,\mathrm{Grp}_{E_\infty}(\textbf{H})
        \cong\mathrm{Sp}^{\mathrm{cn}}(\textbf{H})
    \end{equation}
    (see Remark~\ref{app:rmk:equivalence-einfty-connective}, cf. \cite[Example 1.23]{LurieDAGVII}, \cite[Theorem~5.2.6.10]{lurie2017higher} for the last equivalence) and let $\mathbf M\in\mathrm{ob}\,\mathrm{Sp}^{\mathrm{cn}}(\textbf{H})$ be the corresponding connective
    spectrum under this equivalence. Define
    \begin{equation}
        \mathbf M_{\mathrm{st}}^{h\mathsf H}
        :=
        \mathrm{lim}_{\mathbf{B}\mathsf H}^{\mathrm{Sp}(\textbf{H})}\mathbf M.
    \end{equation}
    Then the connective spectrum corresponding to $M^{h\mathsf H}$ is $        \tau_{\geq0}\left(\mathbf M_{\mathrm{st}}^{h\mathsf H}\right)$. In particular, this means that for every $n\geq0$ there is an equivalence
    \begin{equation}
        \pi_n(M^{h\mathsf H})
        \cong
        \pi_n\left(\mathbf M_{\mathrm{st}}^{h\mathsf H}\right).
    \end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-11 -->
<!-- proof-14: body_md -->
The inclusion $ i:\mathrm{Sp}^{\mathrm{cn}}(\textbf{H})\hookrightarrow\mathrm{Sp}(\textbf{H})$
    has $\tau_{\geq0}$ as its right adjoint. Limits in $\mathrm{Sp}^{\mathrm{cn}}(\textbf{H})$ are
    therefore obtained by taking the corresponding stable limit and then
    applying connective truncation:
    \begin{equation}
        \mathrm{lim}_{\mathbf{B}\mathsf H}^{\mathrm{Sp}^{\mathrm{cn}}(\textbf{H})}\mathbf M
        \cong
        \tau_{\geq0}
        \left(
        \mathrm{lim}_{\mathbf{B}\mathsf H}^{\mathrm{Sp}(\textbf{H})}\mathbf M
        \right).
    \end{equation}
    Under the equivalence $\mathrm{Grp}_{E_\infty}(\textbf{H})\cong\mathrm{Sp}^{\mathrm{cn}}(\textbf{H})$, and using Remark~\ref{rmk:limits-underlying}, the left-hand side
    corresponds to $M^{h\mathsf H}$. Connective truncation does not change
    homotopy sheaves in nonnegative degrees, which gives the equivalence of homotopy sheaves.
<!-- end proof-14 -->
<!-- lemma-12: body_md -->
\label{lem:hfp-ss}
    Suppose that $\mathcal{T}$ is $d$-truncated. Then
    \begin{equation}
        \pi_t\mathbf M=0
        \quad \text{for } t<0 \text{ or } d<t.
    \end{equation}
    The Whitehead--Postnikov filtration of $\mathbf M$ induces a
    strongly convergent spectral sequence (cf.\ \cite[Proposition 7.1.3.19]{lurie2017higher})
    \begin{equation}
        E_1^{s,t}
        =
        H^s(\mathsf H,\pi_t\mathbf M)
        \Longrightarrow
        \pi_{t-s}
        \left(\mathbf M_{\mathrm{st}}^{h\mathsf H}\right),
        \quad
        d_r:E_r^{s,t}\longrightarrow E_r^{s+r+1,\,t+r},
    \end{equation}
    where
    \begin{equation}
        \mathbf M_{\mathrm{st}}^{h\mathsf H}
        =
        \mathrm{lim}_{\mathbf{B}\mathsf H}^{\mathrm{Sp}(\textbf{H})}\mathbf M.
    \end{equation}
    Here, for an $\mathsf H$-equivariant sheaf of abelian groups $A$, we write
    $H^s(\mathsf H,A):=\pi_{-s}\left(\lim^{\mathrm{Sp}(\textbf{H})}_{\mathbf{B}\mathsf H}HA\right)$, with $HA$ the spectrum corresponding to $A$. When
    $\mathsf H$ is $0$-truncated and $A$ is constant, this is the group cohomology
    $H^s_{\rm gp}(\mathsf H,A)$.
<!-- end lemma-12 -->
<!-- proof-15: body_md -->
Since $\mathcal{T}$ is $d$-truncated, so is the internal mapping object $M=[
  \raisebox{1pt}{\rm\normalfont\textesh}
\mathcal{X},\mathcal{T}]$. Since $M$ is a grouplike $E_\infty$-object, the
    corresponding spectrum $\mathbf M$ is connective. Therefore
    \begin{equation}
        \pi_t\mathbf M=0
        \quad\text{for }t<0\text{ and }t>d.
    \end{equation}

    Now, consider the Whitehead tower of $\mathbf M$ in
    $\mathrm{Fun}(\mathbf{B}\mathsf H,\mathrm{Sp}(\textbf{H}))$,
    \begin{equation}
        0=\tau_{\geq d+1}\mathbf M
        \longrightarrow
        \tau_{\geq d}\mathbf M
        \longrightarrow
        \cdots
        \longrightarrow
        \tau_{\geq0}\mathbf M=\mathbf M,
    \end{equation}
    whose cofibers are
    \begin{equation}
        \mathrm{cofib}\left(\tau_{\geq t+1}\mathbf M\to\tau_{\geq t}\mathbf M\right)
        \cong
        \Sigma^tH(\pi_t\mathbf M),
        \quad 0\leq t\leq d.
    \end{equation}
    Since truncation functors are computed pointwise, this is a tower of
    $\mathsf H$-objects, where the cofiber sequences are furthermore equivariant. Stable homotopy fixed points are a limit and therefore preserve
    fiber sequences, which are equivalently cofiber sequences in a stable category.
    Applying $(-)^{h\mathsf H}_{\mathrm{st}}$ to the tower therefore yields
    a filtration of $\mathbf M_{\mathrm{st}}^{h\mathsf H}$ of finite length
    $d+1$, with subquotients
    \begin{equation}
        \left(\Sigma^tH(\pi_t\mathbf M)\right)^{h\mathsf H}_{\mathrm{st}},
        \quad
        \pi_{t-s}
        \left(\Sigma^tH(\pi_t\mathbf M)\right)^{h\mathsf H}_{\mathrm{st}}
        \cong
        H^s\left(\mathsf H,\pi_t\mathbf M\right).
    \end{equation}
    The associated exact couple gives a spectral sequence with the $E_1$-page and differentials as stated, converging to
    $\pi_{t-s}(\mathbf M_{\mathrm{st}}^{h\mathsf H})$. Since $\mathbf M$ is $d$-truncated, the filtration is finite, so the
    spectral sequence degenerates at a finite page and converges strongly.
<!-- end proof-15 -->

(\mathcal{X}

{\mathcal H}),\mathcal{T}]

    (not the stack of pointed maps). 
    Thus, in total degrees $t-s\geq0$, the spectral sequence of Lemma~\ref{lem:hfp-ss} computes the homotopy sheaves of $[
  \raisebox{1pt}{\rm\normalfont\textesh}
(\mathcal{X}
  \IfBooleanTF{#1}
    {\big/\mkern-7mu\big/}
    {/\mkern-6mu/}
{\mathcal H}),\mathcal{T}]$.    In negative total degrees, it computes the negative homotopy sheaves
    of the stable homotopy-fixed-point spectrum rather than homotopy
    sheaves of the grouplike $E_\infty$-object.

\mathcal{X},\mathcal{T}]_{*,\mathsf y}

{\mathcal H})

<!-- remark-27: body_md -->
\label{rmk:hypotheses-fibration}
  It is worthwhile to comment on the role of the various hypotheses in Theorem~\ref{thm:descent-magnetic-symmetries}.
    \begin{itemize}
        \item The assumption that \textbf{$\mathcal{T}$ is a grouplike
        $E_\infty$-object} is used to form the reduced object
        $[
  \raisebox{1pt}{\rm\normalfont\textesh}
\mathcal{X},\mathcal{T}]_{\mathrm{red}}$, to identify it with the pointed mapping
        object via the splitting of Lemma~\ref{lem:stable-retract}, and to
        perform the change of coordinates in Lemma~\ref{lem:pointed-splitting}. Only part (i) is independent of the grouplike $E_\infty$ structure.

        That being said, it would be interesting to explore the existence of a similar splitting for $\mathcal{T}$ an $E_n$-object, in particular whether there is a \textit{semidirect product} splitting.

        \item The \textbf{truncation} hypothesis on $\mathcal{T}$ is used only for
        the spectral-sequence statement in part \textup{(iv)}. Parts
        \textup{(i)}--\textup{(iii)} remain valid without it, but the filtration is then infinite, so convergence must be proven separately.

        \item  The existence of a \textbf{homotopy fixed point}
        $\mathsf y: *\to 
  \raisebox{1pt}{\rm\normalfont\textesh}
\mathcal{X}$ is used only in part
        \textup{(iii)}. It allows one to identify the canonical reduced
        object with the pointed mapping object
        $[
  \raisebox{1pt}{\rm\normalfont\textesh}
\mathcal{X},\mathcal{T}]_{*,\mathsf y}$ and hence to split
        $\mathrm{Mag}_\mathcal{T}(\mathcal{X}
  \IfBooleanTF{#1}
    {\big/\mkern-7mu\big/}
    {/\mkern-6mu/}
{\mathcal H},\bar x)$ as in Lemma~\ref{lem:pointed-splitting}. Without such a homotopy fixed point,
        the canonical fiber sequence of part \textup{(ii)} survives, but
        the splitting statement need not hold.
    \end{itemize}
<!-- end remark-27 -->
<!-- remark-28: body_md -->
\label{rmk:t-independence}
    We remark that Theorem~\ref{thm:descent-magnetic-symmetries} uses no properties of the dualizing stack $\mathcal{T}$ beyond those explicitly stated in the hypotheses. In particular, the fiber sequence of part \textup{(ii)} and the splitting of part \textup{(iii)} hold verbatim for any such $\mathcal{T}$, regardless of any further geometric structure it may encode, such as connections, as in Section~\ref{ssec:factorization-connected-stacks}.

    Specializing to $\mathcal{T}=\mathbf{B}^{d}_{\nabla}U(1)$ makes the resulting statements fully explicit. If, in addition, $
  \raisebox{1pt}{\rm\normalfont\textesh}
\mathcal{X}$ is connected ($\mathbf{B}\mathsf H$ always is), Theorem~\ref{thm:pontryagin-factorization} identifies both $\mathrm{Mag}_{\mathbf{B}^{d}_{\nabla}U(1)}(\mathcal{X})=[
  \raisebox{1pt}{\rm\normalfont\textesh}
\mathcal{X},\mathbf{B}^{d}_{\nabla}U(1)]_*$ and $[\mathbf{B}\mathsf H,\mathbf{B}^{d}_{\nabla}U(1)]_*$ as explicit products of deloopings of Pontryagin duals of integral homology groups, now \textit{discrete}, with homotopy sheaves $\pi_k[
  \raisebox{1pt}{\rm\normalfont\textesh}
\mathcal{X},\mathbf{B}^{d}_{\nabla}U(1)]_*\cong\widehat{H_{d-k}(X,\mathbb{Z})}$ for $0 \leq k \leq d-1$, and similarly for $\mathbf{B}\mathsf H$. Feeding these into the $E_1$-page $E_1^{s,t}=H^s(\mathsf H,\pi_t\mathbf M)$ of part \textup{(iv)} \textit{renders the spectral sequence for $\mathrm{Mag}_{\mathbf{B}^{d}_{\nabla}U(1)}(\mathcal{X} 
  \IfBooleanTF{#1}
    {\big/\mkern-7mu\big/}
    {/\mkern-6mu/}
 \mathcal H)$
computable in terms of the group cohomology} of $\mathsf H$ valued in the Pontryagin
duals $\widehat{H_n(X,\mathbb{Z})}$ and in $\pi_d\mathcal{T}=U(1)$, with one exception. The row $t=0$ of the unpointed mapping stack
$M=[
  \raisebox{1pt}{\rm\normalfont\textesh}
\mathcal{X},\mathcal{T}]$ also contains the constant-summand contribution
\begin{equation}
    \pi_0\mathcal{T}\cong\Omega_{\mathrm{cl}}^{d+1},
\end{equation}
with the trivial $\mathsf H$-action. This contributes
$\Omega_{\mathrm{cl}}^{d+1}$ to $E_1^{0,0}=H^0(\mathsf H,\pi_0M)$, together with
\begin{equation}
    H^s\left(\mathsf H,\Omega_{\mathrm{cl}}^{d+1}\right)
\end{equation}
in negative stems. On each Cartesian probe $U$, the coefficient sheaf
is naturally identified with
$\Omega^d(U)/d\Omega^{d-1}(U)$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:deligne}. It comes from the constant summand $\mathcal{T}$, which drops out of
$\mathrm{Mag}_{\mathbf{B}^{d}_{\nabla}U(1)}$ (cf. the proof of Corollary~\ref{pin:route1}). Alternatively, working with $[
  \raisebox{1pt}{\rm\normalfont\textesh}
\mathcal{X},\mathcal{T}]_{\mathrm{red}}$ as in part \textup{(ii)} removes this row from the start, since $\pi_0[
  \raisebox{1pt}{\rm\normalfont\textesh}
\mathcal{X},\mathcal{T}]_{\mathrm{red}}\cong\widehat{H_d(X,\mathbb{Z})}$.
<!-- end remark-28 -->
